1	# Conformance checks
2	
3	The deterministic-enforcement layer: corpus rules converted into machine-run checks, executed
4	when a session finishes (Stop hook) and in CI. Design and rationale → [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md);
5	which rule came from which instruction → [docs/conversion-inventory.md](../../docs/conversion-inventory.md).
6	Dependency-free Node ≥ 18 — no install step.
7	
8	## Running
9	
10	```sh
11	node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs             # world scope: repo-state rules + settings diagnostics — runs in the test/CI flow
12	node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs              # work scope: rules judging the current change — runs at the Stop hook (--transcript enables the conversation rules)
13	                                                   # the two are independent runners; each accepts --changed (transitional
14	                                                   # adoption-backlog scoping) and --base REF
15	node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list      # machine-readable catalog of every rule, both scopes
16	node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --init      # write .claudinite-checks.json — the baseline plus the fingerprinted packs
17	
18	node --test engine/test/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs skills/*.test.mjs mount/*.test.mjs   # the test suite, as CI runs it
19	```
20	
21	Exit 1 when blocking findings exist; advisory findings never fail a run. In a consuming repo
22	the paths start with `.claudinite/`. The steady state is a repo at zero findings (or reviewed
23	acceptances); `--changed` exists only for adopting a repo with a backlog. **Base-ref note:**
24	delta rules (new suppression markers, commits referencing an issue) and `--changed` scoping
25	diff against the merge-base with `origin/main` (falling back to `origin/master`, `main`,
26	`master`) — and a stale `origin/main` widens that delta, billing the base branch's own
27	commits to the work. So each run **refreshes that ref first** (one `git fetch` of the base
28	branch into its remote-tracking ref — no local branch, index, or working tree is touched).
29	It is best-effort and bounded: no network, no remote, or an unresponsive server and the run
30	continues against the ref as it stands (~10ms to fail, 8s ceiling when a server accepts and
31	stalls; ~0.3s when it succeeds). `CLAUDINITE_CHECKS_NO_FETCH=1` skips it — for a sealed
32	sandbox, or to pin the base deliberately. `squash-merge-history` is one of these delta
33	rules: it scopes to the merge commits the current change introduces since that merge-base,
34	not the repo's whole history, and a merge already on the base branch is filtered out even
35	when a criss-cross or shallow-clone merge-base leaves it inside that range.
36	
37	**Stale-mount note:** a stale mount can likewise surface a spurious finding that an
38	already-merged canon fix would skip — the mount is refreshed by the SessionStart sync hook, so a
39	session that began before the fix landed still runs the older rules. Before committing a
40	workaround for a finding (an `accept` subtree, a suppression pragma), re-run the sync hook and
41	re-check: when the fix is known to have landed upstream, a stale mount is the likelier cause than
42	a real violation.
43	
44	**Vendored/generated files are out of the sweep.** Files git marks `linguist-vendored` or
45	`linguist-generated` in `.gitattributes` — recorded third-party fixtures, machine-written
46	output — are not the project's own code, so the engine drops them from the default file set and
47	**every** check skips them (no per-rule `accept` needed). Mark a subtree vendored/generated
48	rather than accepting each finding it triggers. The one exception is `generated-merge-driver`,
49	which reasons *about* generated files and so still inspects them.
50	
51	## Configuration — `.claudinite-checks.json` (repo root)
52	
53	The declaration is **pack-oriented**: a `packs` entry is a pack id string, or an entry object
54	carrying that pack's own settings — its parameters, and the overrides/exemptions that exist
55	*because* the pack is declared:
56	
57	```json
58	{
59	  "packs": [
60	    "baseline",
61	    { "id": "an-edge-graph-pack",
62	      "config": { "rules": [ { "from": "src", "to": "tests" } ] },
63	      "rules": { "some-rule": "advisory" },
64	      "accept": [ { "rule": "a-rule", "path": "src/shared/", "reason": "..." } ] },
65	    { "id": "a-framework-pack", "via": ["the-class-pack-requiring-it"] }
66	  ],
67	  "rules": { "a-rule": "off" },
68	  "accept": [
69	    { "rule": "a-rule", "path": "src/shared/", "reason": "named cross-cutting concern" }
70	  ],
71	  "maintenance": { "delivery": "auto-merge" }
72	}
73	```
74	
75	- **packs** — the declared packs; the closed set that executes. **No pack runs undeclared** —
76	  the baseline too is declared explicitly (`--init` seeds it; the nightly
77	  the update flows backfill a missing declaration). A declared id may name a **canon** pack (mounted from
78	  `.claudinite/packs/`) or one of the repo's **own local packs** (`.claudinite/local_packs/<id>/` —
79	  discovered from the repo's own tree, `local: true`); both are declared and gated identically. A
80	  local pack's canonical declaration token is **namespaced**: `"local_packs/<id>"` (string entry, or
81	  an entry object's `id`) — self-documenting, and a canon id can never be claimed by accident. The
82	  engine resolves both forms to the bare id ([`packEntryId`](../pack_loader/pack-registry.mjs)), so a bare local
83	  id still activates while the fleet migrates (the update flows rewrite it; the `local-pack-namespace`
84	  baseline migration tracks convergence). An
85	  **unknown** pack name — one that matches neither a canon nor a local pack — is a settings error,
86	  caught at load (see below); a broken or id-colliding local pack.mjs is likewise surfaced as a
87	  blocking `config` finding, never a silent drop. A pack's fingerprint only *suspects* it is wanted
88	  and never forces or forbids its declaration (a local pack is never fingerprinted or seeded — it is
89	  always declared by hand). An entry object carries:
90	  - **id** — the pack name (required; a bare string entry is shorthand for `{ "id": ... }`).
91	  - **config** — the pack's parameters (e.g. the dirs a technology pack's `npm ci` runs in, an
92	    edge-graph pack's edge list). This is the home of what a legacy top-level `packConfig` key
93	    used to hold — the engine still reads that key, but baselining folds it into the entries
94	    and nothing should keep authoring it. The `pack-entry-config` baseline migration
95	    ([engine/migrations/](../migrations/README.md)) documents the fold; once the fleet is off the
96	    old shape, the key stops being a valid setting.
97	  - **answers** — the pack's adoption-interview answers, **verbatim**, keyed by question id
98	    (`{ "<question-id>": "<answer>" }`). A pack declares its questions on its `pack.mjs`; the
99	    unanswered gap surfaces only as a mild SessionStart note (strict solely inside the bootstrap
100	    adoption flow), never a conformance finding —
101	    [packs/README.md](../../packs/README.md#adoption-interview-questions). A stored answer whose
102	    question the pack no longer declares is an *advisory* `config` finding.
103	  - **rules** / **accept** — severity overrides and acceptances **motivated by declaring this
104	    pack**; they may name *any* rule (declaring pack A can require an exemption to pack B's
105	    check), and the entry is their provenance — the file says which declaration required which
106	    exception. Same shapes as the top-level keys; entry-sourced acceptances surface with the
107	    pack named. Two sources disagreeing on a rule's severity is a settings error, never a
108	    silent last-writer-wins.
109	  - **via** — written by the engine (never by hand) when a dependency is materialized:
110	    the declared packs that directly require this one, kept accurate by the update
111	    backfill (an empty recomputed `via` marks an orphan the project can drop).
112	- **rules** — per-rule severity override: `"off"` / `"advisory"` / `"blocking"`. The top-level

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Pattern-check engine: structured-data (parsed JSON/YAML) assertions

The Category-3 append: checks whose subject is a parsed document's fields
become declarations. Documents are parsed at most once per scan (.json via
JSON.parse, .ya?ml via the minimal YAML parser), shared by every rule; an
absent or unparsable document asserts nothing. Field paths are dotted;
presence = value !== undefined.

New spec vocabulary:
- checkParsedFile: where whenFieldPresent holds, requireField must be
  present / forbidField must not;
- equalParsedValues: two parsed fields must be equal — the first file
  selected by a path+content probe, an absent second file and a mismatch
  each firing their own declared message ({first}/{second} interpolate);
- forEachParsedEntry: iterate a document's named entries (e.g. SAM
  Resources) filtered by field equality, forbidding an array value
  ({entry} interpolates the entry name);
- checkKeyValueFile: dotenv-style schema — file exists, KEY=value lines
  only, closed key set, every key declared ({key}/{keys}/{line});

input.body:
Closes #819. The Category-3 append, following the pattern round (#790) and the cross-file tree round (#800): checks whose subject is a **parsed document's fields** are now declarations.

## Engine

Documents are parsed **at most once per scan** — `.json` via `JSON.parse`, `.ya?ml` via the existing minimal YAML parser — through a cache shared by the whole rule family, keeping the one-pass economics. An absent or unparsable document asserts nothing (matching every original check's catch-and-skip posture). Field paths are dotted (`devDependencies.esbuild`); a field counts as present when its value is not `undefined`.

Four new assertion kinds, named to read without the design doc:

- **`checkParsedFile`** — `{ file, whenFieldPresent, requireField | forbidField, what, fix }`: where the guard field is present, another field must be present / absent.
- **`equalParsedValues`** — two parsed fields must be equal; the first file is selected by a path + content probe (`filesMatching` + `whereFileContains`, reproducing `findExtensionManifest`), an absent second file fires `whenSecondMissing` at its own path, and a mismatch fires `whenUnequal` at the first file with `{first}`/`{second}` interpolated.
- **`forEachParsedEntry`** — iterate a document's named entries (e.g. SAM `Resources`) filtered by `whereFieldEquals`, forbidding a value in an array field (`ignoreCase` supported); `{entry}` interpolates the entry name.
- **`checkKeyValueFile`** — dotenv-style schema: the file must exist, hold only `KEY=value` lines and `#` comments, use only the declared keys, and declare every one — each failure mode with its own declared message (`{key}`/`{keys}`/`{line}`).

Plus two relevance gates: `someTrackedFileContains: { pathMatching, text }` and `exactlyOneTrackedFileMatches`.

## Converted (4)

- `cer/version-sync` → `equalParsedValues`
- `cer/release-config` → `checkKeyValueFile`
- `aws-sam/cloudfront-authorization` → `forEachParsedEntry`
- `aws-sam/esbuild-dependency` → gates + `checkParsedFile`

All ids, severities, and message strings preserved verbatim. That brings the corpus to **20 checks as declarations** across the three rounds.

## Deliberately kept as code

- `firebase/functions-node-pin` + `functions-predeploy-build` — a two-document join (firebase.json codebases → each source dir's package.json) through the shared `functionsCodebases` lib; a join/query vocabulary isn't worth its weight for two rules.
- `aws-sam/handler-path` — a derived comparison (Handler prefix vs EntryPoints dirname with skip conditions), needs expressions.
- `growth-config` — validates the in-memory loaded config, with per-field bespoke prose.
- `cer/privacy-permission-alignment` — shares `requestedPermissions` with the work-scoped `permission-added-store-issue`; one extraction, one home (converting one side would split that source of truth).
- `web-speech-no-window-api-in-service-worker` — needs a parsed-field→file-set feed into `matchLines`; noted as a possible follow-up.

## Testing

- Engine suite grown to 21 tests: each new kind's firing and silent sides, parse-failure tolerance, gate behavior, and a parse-once assertion via a read counter.
- See-it-fail: three mutations (dropping the `whereFieldEquals` filter, inverting the equality compare, dropping the unknown-key check) each made the suite go red before restoring.
- Full suite: **1561/1561 pass**, including the aws-sam and chrome-extension-release pack tests that pin all four converted checks.
- `check_the_world` on this repo: identical with and without the change (0 blocking, same 28 pre-existing advisories).

Category 3 is built and delivered: **PR #820** — https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/820 (closes #819), CI queued and running on it.

What it adds, in the same one-pass engine:

- **Parsed-document infrastructure**: each `.json`/`.ya?ml` file is parsed at most once per scan through a cache shared by the whole rule family; absent or unparsable documents assert nothing (the same catch-and-skip posture every original check had).
- **Four self-describing assertion kinds**: `checkParsedFile` (where field X is present, require/forbid field Y), `equalParsedValues` (two parsed fields must agree, with per-failure-mode messages and `{first}`/`{second}` interpolation), `forEachParsedEntry` (iterate SAM-style `Resources` entries filtered by `Type`, forbid an array value, `{entry}` interpolates), and `checkKeyValueFile` (dotenv schema: closed key set, every key required, per-failure-mode messages). Plus two gates: `someTrackedFileContains` and `exactlyOneTrackedFileMatches`.
- **Four checks converted** with messages verbatim: `cer/version-sync`, `cer/release-config`, `aws-sam/cloudfront-authorization`, `aws-sam/esbuild-dependency` — the corpus now has 20 declarative checks across the three rounds.

Two judgment calls worth knowing about: I kept `cer/privacy-permission-alignment` as code because it shares the `requestedPermissions` extraction with its work-scoped sibling — converting one side would split a single source of truth in two. And I started to export `release-config`'s key list from the vendored `read-config.mjs` stub to deduplicate it, then reverted: importing that stub executes its top-level Action logic (it `process.exit`s), so the declaration keeps its own key list exactly as the original check did.

Verified: 1,561/1,561 tests pass (engine suite now 21 tests, three mutations each confirmed to bite), and the repo's conformance sweep is identical with and without the change.
